title.value: Individual Fairness in Kidney Exchange Programs
title.justification: The paper focuses on achieving individual fairness in Kidney Exchange Programs (KEPs).
title.quote: In this paper, the existence of multiple optimal plans for a KEP is explored as a mean to achieve individual fairness.

analysis.description: The paper focuses on proposing new methodologies for ensuring individual fairness in Kidney Exchange Programs (KEPs) by designing randomized policies for selecting optimal solutions. This ensures all patients have equal opportunity to receive a transplant. Several novel methods, including integer and constraint programming approaches, are proposed and evaluated.

type.justification: The paper involves computational experiments and evaluates methods for achieving individual fairness in kidney exchanges.
type.quote: The advantages of our proposed method over the common practice of using the optimal solution obtained by a solver are stressed through computational experiments.

name.justification: The paper discusses decision-making algorithms in the context of kidney exchange programs.
name.quote: KEP is an example of algorithmic decision making with a significant impact on the lives of individuals.

name.justification: The paper applies optimization techniques in the context of healthcare, specifically kidney exchanges.
name.quote: The goal of KEPs is to determine a set of disjoint chains and cycles representing the kidney exchanges to be performed such that the benefit of the patients receiving a transplant is maximized.

name.justification: The paper uses Integer Linear Programming (ILP) to model kidney exchange problems.
name.quote: We present and evaluate alternative methods for enumerating the solutions of KEPs, using Integer Linear Programming (ILP) and Constraint Programming (CP).

name.justification: The paper demonstrates methods using Constraint Programming for efficient solution enumeration in KEPs.
name.quote: We present and evaluate alternative methods for enumerating the solutions of KEPs, using Integer Linear Programming (ILP) and Constraint Programming (CP).
